Hi [~accountid:712020:636564c7-70de-4b2e-a4e4-de1202946f82] and [~accountid:619f414fd5986c006ae26999] 

Overall, the agreement is fine, but there are several clauses and sections that should be either changed or addressed. Please see my comments below (also discussed this already with Birgit over a call).

# Clauses 3.3 and 3.4 establish an exclusivity clause. However, at the beginning of the agreement it has been marked “N/A” for both the Exclusivity Period and Competitors. I conclude from this that the exclusivity clause does not apply to this agreement. If this is correct, then clauses 3.3 and 3.4 should be removed as they are not relevant and would otherwise cause unnecessary confusion.
# The agreement includes several clauses that set out the process of service provision in a very specific manner. Following these clauses would hinder normal business operations and make day-to-day marketing quite difficult, especially considering this agreement is for rather straight-forward marketing activities. It would be great if Saku could explain if the following clauses are actually relevant in practice and we are expected to follow them exactly:
## Clause 5.3: Supplier shall not incorporate and/or use Third Party Materials in any Deliverable unless Supplier has obtained the prior written approval of Customer to do so.
## Clause 5.4: Supplier shall give Customer reasonable prior notice of its intention to include any Third Party Materials in any Deliverable and at the same time shall notify Customer in writing.
## The entirety of section 8 (Change Control).

# Clause 6.1.4 establishes a requirement to follow the Health and Safety requirements. Taking into account that this agreement is directed at marketing, why is this relevant and why would a breach of this clause count as a material breach?
# Clause 9.9 and 9.9.2 establishes that Saku can recover from Bolt any costs reasonably incurred by Saku in obtaining substitute services from a third party, if Bolt is unable or unwilling in Saku’s reasonable opinion to provide the Service/Deliverables. This can create claims the amount of which is impossible to foresee. I suggest either removing clause 9.9.2 or removing the “in Customer's reasonable opinion” part from clause 9.9
# Section 13 (Intellectual Property) - as I understand, the Deliverables may also include images of Saku products which in turn will include Saku’s IP. Bolt should get a license from Saku to use such IP for the duration of agreement and for the express purpose of providing the Services.
# Clause 13.2.1 states that Saku shall own all Intellectual Property Rights in the Deliverables produced by Bolt. While clause 13.10 specifies how Bolt Background IP is licensed, then the wording of 13.2.1 leaves room for a different interpretation, meaning Saku would own elements of Bolt’s CVI if these are used in the Deliverables. I would specify this and reword 13.2 as follows: “Customer shall own all Intellectual Property Rights in the Deliverables produced by Supplier {color:#ff5630}during and for the express purpose of fulfilling this Agreement{color}.“
# Clause 13.3 has the same issue and should be reworded as follows: “Supplier hereby irrevocably, unconditionally and absolutely assigns to Customer, with full title guarantee and free from all third party rights, all right, title and interest in and to all existing and future Intellectual Property Rights (including future copyright and design right) subsisting in or relating to all Assigned Materials -whether- created, developed or produced {color:#ff5630}for the express purpose and during the performance of this Agreement {color}-before, on or after the Commencement Date,- in all countries and with the right to sue for damages and other relief for past infringement of any of those Intellectual Property Rights.  For the avoidance of doubt, the assignment under this Clause shall take effect from the date on which the relevant Assigned Material was or is created, developed or produced.“
# Clause 13.10 – the purpose of use for Bolt Background IPR is not specified. It should be limited to the extent necessary to use the Deliverables. Otherwise Saku would essentially be allowed to remove the Background IPR from the Deliverables and use it separately for its own business purposes.
# If section 17 (Insurance) is crossed out because it is not relevant, then I suggest just removing its text.
# I would reword clause 21.3 as follows: “Supplier shall -at all times- {color:#ff5630}during the provision of the Services{color} comply with the Carlsberg Group’s Supplier and Licensee Code of Conduct from time to time in force, the latest version of which is set out in Schedule 7 and is available at [https://www.carlsberggroup.com/who-we-are/about-the-carlsberg-group/integrated-supply-chain/|https://www.carlsberggroup.com/who-we-are/about-the-carlsberg-group/integrated-supply-chain/] and which Supplier hereby confirms it has read and accepts.
# We should make clause 23.2 mutual, as Bolt also operates as a group and may need to include one or more of its entities to perform the agreement from time to time.



If Saku does not back down from the Health and Safety requirements clause, then we should check if we can follow these at all or not - since this isn’t exactly legal in nature, it should be reviewed by someone from Bolt who deals with health and safety requirements daily.

Furthermore, we should compare their Code of Conduct to ours and see if there are any key differences there.

Hi [~accountid:712020:f0e74860-330c-44ed-9e8f-e89de3fd8d5c], 

We have reviewed the employment contract and there are a few things to note in this situation. It is clear that the app that Stefan created was for work purposes only, as this app is directly related to the workflow and requirements dictated by the German municipalities. During our call, I asked why he didn’t get someone from Bolt to create this app and the response provided was along the lines that it would have been too slow. Therefore Stefan took the proactive approach in creating this app outside of work hours (Saturday) and through his own Dev account. 



The position is clear for us that Bolt should be the owner of this app. The relevant IP clauses in the employment contract that Stefan signed is set out further below. Clause 10.1 outlines that all work created by the employee is automatically assigned to Bolt, “to the extent they are related to his duties under the Employment Contract also outside of his working hours”. The general position is that anything created automatically vests into Bolt. 



By using his own personal Dev Account and to use potentially sensitive data could be viewed as breaching our [+Acceptable use policy+|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/BILP/pages/2100167797/Acceptable+use+policy]. In this case, however, I don’t view these actions as being sinister, rather I would keep the tone more focused on being proactive, which is something that Bolt should favour. Although, the best approach should be proactive within the boundaries of our relevant policies and guidelines. 



*Next steps*



We will need to transfer this app from Stefan’s personal Dev account into the Bolt ecosystem. There are many issues if this continues to be from his personal account and also places some risk/liability onto Stefan, particularly when dealing with the various forms of data. 

From a technical standpoint, I am not able to advise on this process, however I assume that it is relatively straightforward to move apps from one account to another. If not, perhaps this is something that Bolt could replicate under our own Dev account. 



I would also recommend that we pay Stefan a small fee, as a gesture of goodwill, say EUR1500. Although we are not obligated to pay any such fee, I think that this could go a long way. This will be up to the manager to confirm and arrange with the People Partner. 



Please let me know if you wish to discuss this further.

Kind regards,

Ken

yes, the term is a interchangeable in our side. take rate with commission. 

So we’d like to first test supply elasticity, where 5% of population of our drivers will get a take rate of 5% higher (means -5% less earnings), 5% will get a take rate of -5% less (means 5% higher earnings), and 5% will get a take rate of -10% (means 10% higher earnings) to learn how drivers will react on their income changes. and 75% of drivers population won’t have any change (control group). 

Once we get the supply elasticity test data, we’ll combine it with our demand elasticity test result we already have, test what we call as ‘dynamic commission’, where it’ll be a combination of higher/lower prices to riders with higher/lower earnings to drivers. something that Uber also have been doing seamlessly and a point that they’re thriving in and benefit their drivers, but we’re still in the learning process on having such feature. Hence the plan to have the test. 

We’re currently running the supply elasticity test already in London and would like to expand this to Manchester & Birmingham. 



Hope this clears it up!

I think Workday currently only matches the EndtoEnd ID with the payment ID in Workday.

To solve it would be to add to Workday additional logic when processing pain002 messages, that will also check some other information in addition to reference, such as amount and date.

Hi! As Piotr correctly said, having AR as a metric is risky from the reclassification side, since if we impose such harsh requirements, then the courts can find that we are essentially controlling couriers ourselves. To clarify, just because the fleet is the employer “on paper”, the courts can still find that since Bolt is imposing control mechanisms on couriers, we can be deemed as (co-)employers. This is also supported by the PWD (not in force yet) article 3, that says that even if intermediaries (i.e. fleets) are used, then couriers can still be found Bolt’s employees if the conditions for employee-employer relationship are fulfilled. 

Having an AR requirement (especially as high as 70%) is one of the riskiest measures that can used, since this will be seen as “imposing control”, which is one of the conditions for classifying couriers as employees. 

Recommendation from Product Legal would be to use less risky requirements, e.g. bonuses on number of deliveries made. They are understandably not as efficient to ensure quality supply, but they will significantly reduce the risk.

h3. *What compliance checks are and how to handle them*

Sometimes, Citibank and Wise (our payment providers) may ask us to provide additional details regarding drivers, companies, couriers and providers. It is a normal practice by the payment providers (e.g Citibank, Wise) to contact the payment sender (Bolt). A compliance check request is always related to a particular payout and we usually have two weeks to provide these details.

The purpose of a compliance check is to prevent terrorist financing and money laundering, and the legal basis for these is AML (anti-money laundering regulations). Section 11 of our standard T&Cs contain information on AML. These checks do not violate GDPR or any other regulations regarding personal data as we do not store the data, do not share it with any third parties and do not use it for any other purposes.

These details may include a full name, date and place of birth and nationality of a private person or a full name, legal address, line of business and ownership details.

Compliance checks are received by the Partner payments team and forwarded on to the payment receiver to the email address in the partner’s profile. At times, the payments team seeks help from the local operations team/CS team, who then should try to reach the partner and explain the purpose of the compliance check in their native language.

If the partner does not provide the requested details on time, the payout will be returned to Bolt or blocked by the bank.

Hello All, 

*Technical details:*

Due to the Hungarian regulations and our limitations we are not able to fiscalise invoices with Bolt Admin. Therefore no invoices is being issued via the Bolt system on behalf of the Driver (except for Bolt Business clients where we rely on third party fiscalisation) after the rides.

To issue invoices on behalf of the Driver Bolt System would have to be a certified invoicing system with real time connection to the hu tax authorities. 

*Invoice:*
Riders are able to ask for an invoice at the end of the ride. It is a common issue that Riders believe they will receive an invoice automatically as they do it other countries and not aware that they should request it in the car after their ride.

Rider TC is stating that users should request an invoice in the car , however the Rider TC is only available in Hungarian and usually not read by Riders.

*Possible solution for this case:*
CS can check with the Drivers if they are willing to issue an invoice retrospectively however a little bit too much time has passed. We will update you if we can successfully obtain it.
I would avoid standing out the “Statement” document as they are not considered invoices in Hungary and WizzAir will not accept it.

*Solution for the future*

# We should roll out the English-Hungarian Rider Terms and Conditions that are based on HQ’s global TC and slightly modified due to the special local environment. This has been send to HQ legal team multiple times and waiting for approval. Any advancement here would be highly appreciated.

# We could try to introduce a floating banner in the Rider app bringing the users attention to the invoicing maybe together with a blog post. This step is being evaluated now.

Hi [~accountid:63a00ef0f3e7004f77fadf98] ,

Normally on business resale the amount invoiced to and from Bolt is the same, save in case of a VAT reverse-charge, as then the local VAT is not included in the invoice.

 [~accountid:625fb4941046bb0071ddf44a] deals with B4B VAT, and she is much abler than I am to go into the details of the model.

Regarding the example at hand, I have a couple of questions:

# Is the cost of this promo-code borne by Bolt or business customer?
# If borne by business customer, was it used on a ride by someone outside the business customer or is business customer paying for the full value (ride + promo-code)?
# And since we are dealing with the resale model, not the intermediate one, would it be an issue for Accounting if promo-code is only mentioned as a payment method in the invoice from Bolt to business customers? In such a case the trip invoice from driver to Bolt would be for the full trip price, as if no promo-code was applicable, while the invoice from Bolt to business customer would add the promo-code as paid by.

Hey, [~accountid:712020:0b1ccfcb-3809-460a-88ab-c96985ba329a] - please find the preliminary investigation into the issue. If you have any questions, I am willing to answer them. Additionally, what would be the recommendations on how to proceed with this case?



*~ I. Summary of the events ~*

On August 29, 2024, a Bolt driver mistakenly shared his One-Time Password with an individual who falsely promised to add all vehicle categories to his profile. This led to the unauthorised access of the driver's account, during which the fraudster altered the driver's email address and phone number. The incident was discovered and reported on the same day. he fraudster had access to the account for over two days, during which time they made changes to the contact information. The situation is no longer ongoing. 

*~ II. Questions to be answered ~*

# *What data was accessed?*

The driver's email address and phone number were accessed and changed by the fraudster.

# *How the account was accessed - was it a malfunction of our systems or processes, or was it the user’s actions that caused it?*

The account was accessed due to the user’s actions. The driver willingly shared his OTP with a stranger, allowing unauthorised access.

# *Has the user suffered any harm/loss (e.g. financial loss, data has been leaked, etc.)*

Reportedly, the user did not suffer any financial loss. The fraudster did not alter any banking details or withdraw any funds. There is no indication that any other data was leaked.

# *What mitigation steps have been undertaken?*

Immediate steps were taken to mitigate the damage: all devices were logged off, and the original email and phone number were restored. The driver was advised to change his password and cautioned against sharing his OTP in the future.

*~ III. Admin’s Portal Investigation ~*

# The driver claims to be using Samsung A32, which logged onto the account on February 6, 2024. A total number of 14 devices have accessed the account since that date, with 11 of them logging in after August 9, 2024. We were contacted on August 29, 2024, which suggests that the individual may have lost access to the account on that date. Notably, between August 29 and 30, 2024, five new devices were logged into the account.
# Are we changing numbers and email addresses just like that, without an additional verification - [https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/430791021|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/430791021] + [https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/430611312|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/430611312]? If so, should not we address this issue with CS/ change the procedures?
# No data other than email address and phone number seem to have been changed. The driver claimed in this Beehive communication issued on September 3, 2024 ([https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/433043061|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/433043061]), that the hacker was able to change the details, however, the [change logs|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/fleet/drivers/edit/5283840?tab=changeLogs&filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A25%2C%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%22start_time%22%3A1724360400%7D%7D] do not show any ‘car removal' activity between 29-31 August, 2024. Such an activity only took place on September 2, 2024.
# The [main beehive|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/430612491] ticket, the driver claims that his account has been hacked alongside this message (screenshot below) - would not that be a *phishing case*? The address email with '[southafrica-driver.|http://southafrica-driver.eu][*eu*|http://southafrica-driver.eu]*' looks suspicious,* but it is to be confirmed.

!image-20240904-120437.png|width=33.333333333333336%,alt="image-20240904-120437.png"!

*~ IV. Proposed Actions ~*

# Requesting mix-panels of the devices logged into the account to check the IP-addresses and locations of the sign-ins.
# I would like to confirm where such a number of devices comes from with the driver. I suggest scheduling a call with him to confirm if the above-mentioned Samsung A32 is the only device that he has using for the past couple of months or he also was using other devices.
# Completing a Data Breach Assessment may seem necessary.

*~ V. Planned actions ~*

As discussed with Alon, we simply need to record the breach in our Cognito form - making it clear that this was a phishing incident due to the fault of the Driver and that it was promptly resolved by CS following our procedures.

A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund.

~ *I. Summary of the events* ~

The nature of this issue is fragmented and involves multiple Beehive tickets. Chronologically, they include:

a. 19.08.2024 - [First Communication |https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/425850351]- the driver asked why he cannot go online and start using the platform (According to customer support, he had just submitted his vehicle application, which was still pending confirmation, and the safety department had instructed him to run checks on his old car). He sent a picture of himself with a car in the background, asked to be called, but did not answer. 

b. 26.08.2024 - [Second communication|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/432212632] - the driver requested changing his bank account details. The CS agent then requests sending a bank statement meeting the following criteria:

* Your bank account statement in *_Pdf_* form not older than 3 months. ( It should not be cropped and should contain the bank stamp on it).
* Account name must contain your full name (first, middle, last name with no initials).
* Add the account type (savings or current). All requested details should be clear and visible.

An individual firstly sends a bank statement belonging to a different person, not himself, in a non-pdf format. Having pointed this out by CS agent, an individual sends a bank statement with no bank stamp on it. {color:#bf2600}*Eventually, the bank details get updated*{color}{color:#4c9aff}*.*{color}{color:#4c9aff} {color}

c. 29.08.2024 - 11:10 - 16:22 - [Third communication|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/430568094] - the driver initially asks for changing his pin number, then change of his phone number to 0699456564. The phone number gets changed. 

d. [Fourth communication|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/430555884] - 16:52 - 16:58 the driver requests changing his phone number to 0791903022. The phone number gets changed.

e. [Fifth communication|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/431290068] - the driver requests changing his phone number to 0727100796 and change of his email address to [siyamaziya19@gmail.com|http://siyamaziya19@gmail.com/]. Phone and number get changed. Subsequently, the driver requests: ‘_Please note that I must be contacted via email before any changes are made to my phone number or email address_’. Our agent asked for clarification of this, however, received no response. 

f. 29.08.2024 - [Sixth communication|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/430765335] - the driver requested changing his email address to [muanowashu002@gmail.com|http://muanowashu002@gmail.com/]. It was changed. 

g. 01.09.2024 - [Seventh Communication|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/432391032] - the driver requested changing his phone number to 0637200985, claiming he lost access to his phone. Then, shortly after, he claims that everything is sorted and no more changes are needed. 

h. 30.08.2024 - [Ninth Communication|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/431170884] - The driver requested changing the phone number to 0727100796 and change email address to [siyamaziya19@gmail.com|http://siyamaziya19@gmail.com/]. CS claimed that he already had issued such a request and it was fulfilled. 

i. 01.09.2024 - 12:47 - [Tenth Communication|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/432271250] - the driver requested changing his email address to [vhuhonehawe002@gmail.com|http://vhuhonehawe002@gmail.com/]. Then, after several minutes, he withdraws his request, asking for changing the email back and claiming that it was done by mistake. 

j. 01.09.2024 - 13:06 - [Eleventh Communication|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/432212632] - initially, the driver requests changing his email address to [muanowashu002@gmail.com|http://muanowashu002@gmail.com/], however, after 3 minutes, *he claims that someone hacked his account and asks for not changing his account details*. Bolt's representative, Amarachi Ibeh, asked Peter to confirm if he used certain devices (Samsung SM-A135F, Samsung SM-A115F, and Xiaomi 23028RN4DG) and if he had shared his details or one-time password with anyone. Peter confirmed using a Xiaomi device and mentioned that someone he knows may have accessed his account by emailing themselves a link. He reiterated that his account details were fine and should not be altered.

~ *Short Summary of the most crucial part* ~

A driver suspected that an unauthorised individual might have gained access to their Bolt account and attempted to request changes. The incident was reported on September 1, 2024.

Precautionary measures were taken to safeguard the account. All tokens associated with the recently logged-in device were revoked, and the phone number and email address linked to the account were reverted to their original state. The user was advised to change their passwords and was cautioned against sharing One-Time Passwords (OTPs) with others.

~ *II. Questions to be answered* ~

# *What data was accessed?*

Presumably, the fraudster had access to the account. 

# *How the account was accessed - was it a malfunction of our systems or processes, or was it the user’s actions that caused it?*

It is not confirmed how the account was accessed. There is no evidence to suggest a malfunction of the systems or processes. The user suggested that someone they know might have accessed their account by emailing themselves a link. This implies that the access may have been due to the user’s actions or circumstances involving someone they know, rather than a system failure.

# *Has the user suffered any harm/loss (e.g. financial loss, data has been leaked, etc.)*

Reportedly, the user did not suffer any financial loss, however, the banking details have been changed on August 26, 2024. Thus,  the changes noted encompassed the alteration of the email address, banking details and phone number associated with the account (email address and phone numbers multiple times). As for now, there is no indication that any data was leaked or that the user suffered other forms of harm.

# *What mitigation steps have been undertaken?*

* All tokens associated with the recently logged-in device were revoked.
* The email address and phone number were reverted to their original state.
* The user was advised to change their passwords and warned not to share their One-Time Passwords (OTPs) with others.

~ *III. Admin’s Portal investigation* ~

# Since December 2023, 28 different devices have been logged onto the account. Although the claim on the ‘hacked account’ appeared for the first time on the September 9, 2024, it is highly likely that an unauthorised access to the account took place for the first time way earlier. 
# The same question again - is it our standard procedure to accept requests for changing details of the account solely on the basis of a Beehive communciation, without any further verification? Additionally, do not the CS agents have the visibility/ a communicate showing up that multiple requests have been issued in the span of previous several days or even hours?
# The *banking details have been changed* on the 26.08.2024 - it seems crucial to confirm if the bank details belong to the driver. 
# It seems that 2 devices are still having access to the account. Perhaps, an additional sign-out is recommended considering that the driver admitted to be using only the Xiaomi device.
!image-20240904-115425.png|width=81.3563975837452%,alt="image-20240904-115425.png"!

*~ IV. Proposed Actions ~*

# Requesting mix-panels of the devices logged into the account to check the IP-addresses and locations of the sign-ins. 
# Requesting an information if any OTP were triggered in August and September 2024. 
# Arranging a call to the driver to inquiry about the events of the above/ whether he provided access to the other individuals. Furthermore, it seems necessary to confirm whether the newly-determine banking details belong to his bank account.

~ V. Conclusions ~

Dear Berhane,

Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on 6 August 2024.

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, the law requires a data controller such as ourselves to protect the rights of third parties (including the rights of passengers). Furthermore, we must point out that we are not required to disclose documents or otherwise provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

We will share copies of the personal data we hold about you to which you are entitled, in particular:

* Your order history between 24 November 2023 and 23 February 2024

To the extent that you require additional information relating to specific trips, we refer you to the Driver Portal available at [https://partners.bolt.eu/login?isPasswordReset=true&shortlink=lvew0z3s&c=Global|https://partners.bolt.eu/login?isPasswordReset=true&shortlink=lvew0z3s&c=Global], where you can find invoices issued to riders from you as a driver; invoices issued to you as a driver by Bolt; pay statements and balance reports.

For information on how we process relevant personal data, we refer you to our privacy notice available at [https://bolt.eu/en-gb/privacy/privacy-for-drivers/?category=rides|https://bolt.eu/en-gb/privacy/privacy-for-drivers/?category=rides], which includes further information about:

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;
* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.

*Your rights* 

You have the right to request rectification or erasure of personal data or restriction of processing of personal data concerning you or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You have the right to complain directly to the appropriate supervisory authority and seek a judicial remedy. 

If you have any additional questions, please let us know.

Yours sincerely,

*Bolt Privacy Team*

A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin. 
Rides: refund_payments, customer_support_beehive_ridehailing_order_refund
Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days
Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund.

If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

# *Scope of the policy:*

* geographical: list of countries where Bolt has offices and whether there are local specific requirements (e.g. to have the policy translated into the local language ect)
* material: who is covered by this policy (employee, interns, contractors, others?)

# *Check how data processing has changed between 2019 and 2024:*

* in what systems do we store the data (Workday, some feedback systems ect)
* check what *new data points* we started collecting since 2019 (e.g. any changes in employment law obligations, or whether new company wide policies have been enacted (some of the examples would include (i) a policy for diversity and inclusion, where we would start collecting health data to ensure the employees with special needs having full support in Bolt offices but this is not covered in our outdated policy; or (ii) an attendance policy where we would start processing logs not just for safety and security purposes but also for monitoring purposes but since the policy is outdated this is not reflected; other examples)
* check what data points we do not collect any more (e.g. the employment law has changed and we do not need it anymore, or we changed the policies, procedures as a company)
* check the purposes for data processing and make sure they are still accurate
* add new purpose for data processing (monitoring , any types of automated decision making , ect?)
* check whether legal bases remain the same for old data points (old means those which we collected and are still collecting)
* define legal bases for new data points

# *Check the accuracy of security measures implemented to data and whether they need to be updated*
# *Check whether there are procedures in place to ensure that data subject’s rights can be exercised*
# *Check the retention periods depending on jurisdiction where the office is located*

FAQ

Q: Can the Payment OPS issue a refund? 
A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin.

Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

Hi team,

https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360016883020

FAQ

Q: Can the Payment OPS issue a refund? 
A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin. 
Rides: refund_payments, customer_support_beehive_ridehailing_order_refund
Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days
Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin. 
Rides: refund_payments, customer_support_beehive_ridehailing_order_refund
Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days
Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

Hi [~accountid:641d5e830e6828ab20269e6d] - I have had a chance to do a bit more research into this / review it in more detail (only from the *erasure* side for now), and my updated thoughts are below. Let’s discuss on tomorrow’s sync.

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
{color:#4c9aff}*IN SUMMARY*{color}:

* The current process (i.e., where fleet driver requests account deletion, we ask for the fleet’s agreement, and if this is denied we instruct the driver to contact the fleet) *needs to change*. If we use this as a _default_ position for all fleet driver account erasure requests going forward, this would be difficult to defend in the event of an investigation.
* Ultimately, the rights of the data subject trump Bolt’s interest in maintaining good relationships with fleets. As such, if we receive an account erasure request from a fleet driver, *our default position should be to action that request*, as Bolt is under a legal obligation to do so (i.e., we should not rely on fleet approval to action these requests).
* However, I appreciate that Bolt should avoid damaging its relationships with fleets. As such, a solution here could be to *_schedule_* *the account for deletion after a certain period has expired* (e.g., 30 days), *and at the same time* *_flag to the fleet_* *that Bolt is doing so* (i.e., instead of seeking the fleet’s _approval,_ Bolt instead just makes the fleet _aware_ in good time). This would give the fleet an opportunity to get its own ducks in a row (e.g., ensure that any outstanding matters with the driver are settled / that the fleet has the information it needs to do so) before the account is deleted, which would mitigate the risk of a fleet accusing Bolt of helping a driver avoid settling a debt.
* However, I think we need to *bottom-out some fact-finding* on this before we commit to a position. It may also be worth *getting external counsel’s view*, given there are not many obvious precedents that we can rely on here.
{panel}

I appreciate there are also broader questions here regarding the fleet’s role in the context of other data subject access requests, but hopefully this gives us some ideas to get us going. I include some more details on my analysis below.

----

*Issue 1 - Does Article 17 apply in these cases, such that Bolt needs to consider these requests?*

Yes, as Bolt is the data controller. I assume that Bolt is an independent controller in relation to fleets - {color:#4c9aff}*have we ever done any formal analysis on this*{color}?

In the absence of additional context, it would be difficult to argue that Article 17 does not apply to a fleet driver’s deletion request (e.g., on the grounds that the processing is still “_necessary_” or that Bolt has an “_overriding interest_”), as ultimately this mainly comes down to Bolt’s interest in maintaining a good relationship with fleets, which would be a difficult position to defend.

----

*Issue 2 - Can Bolt* +*clearly*+ *rely on an exemption to refuse the deletion request, such that we can seek the fleet’s approval in all cases as a default position?*

IMO, no. Although there are of course additional exemptions under local laws, the exemptions in Article 17(3) GDPR would be difficult to apply as a _default_ position. In particular:

* +Legal obligation+ (Art.17(3)(b)): I am not aware of any additional legal obligations that Bolt could rely on here (beyond any that Bolt would already be relying on to retain certain types of data after _all_ account deletion requests, for example tax obligations). Again, local laws may have some nuances here, but I am not sure this is likely. {color:#4c9aff}*It might also be worth getting local counsel’s views on this*{color}.
* +Legal proceedings+ (Art.17(3)(e)): I have done some quick research on this, and (unsurprisingly) few obvious precedents are directly relevant here. However, where a refusal to uphold a deletion request is upheld, this is usually because there was a more obvious reason to do so than we have on these facts (e.g., litigation was contemplated with the controller, or criminal investigation was feasible). {color:#4c9aff}*It might also be worth getting local counsel’s views on this*{color}.

Context may always alter this analysis (e.g., the fleet driver is requesting that we delete their account, and they are the subject of an ongoing dispute with Bolt about violations of Bolt’s terms), but I doubt that Bolt would be able to clearly rely on an exemption in all cases as a _default_ position. As such, if we were to always seek fleet approval for fleet driver account erasure requests, and an regulator launched an investigation into this, I think we would have a tough time defending this position by citing the provisions of Article 17 GDPR. Ultimately, I think it is more likely that our actions could be interpreted as delaying / thwarting the data subject’s rights.

I should also flag that this analysis relies on the assumption that, operationally speaking, we can only delete accounts wholesale (and cannot pick and choose which parts to delete, such that we could delete the account but retain certain information that a fleet might need). {color:#4c9aff}*Let me know if this is incorrect*{color}.

----

*Issue 3 - How do we keep the fleets happy?*

A solution here may be to shift the focus from asking for the fleet’s _approval_ to making sure that the fleet is _aware_ that this is happening - that way, if there is an ongoing dispute between the fleet and the fleet driver, the fleet will have a chance to organise the information that they need before the account is deleted. This would mitigate the risk of a fleet accusing Bolt of assisting a fleet driver in avoiding paying a debt.

If there was an overriding / legal reason why Bolt should _not_ delete the account (beyond what Bolt is already aware of), this would also put the onus on the fleet to flag this to Bolt, so that we could consider it in the rare cases in which it may apply.

----

*Issue 4 - So what would the process look like?*

The revised process could look like this:

# The fleet driver writes to Bolt and asks for their account to be deleted.
# Bolt responds to the fleet driver promptly, saying that the account *will be scheduled for deletion in accordance with Bolt’s policies and practices*.
# Bolt reaches out to the fleet to notify them that the fleet driver has requested the deletion of their account. This notification would contain both: (a) a reminder that should the fleet continue to require any information after the deletion of the account, it should make arrangements to ensure it has such information; and (b) a request to flag to Bolt any reason why account deletion would be an issue (if applicable), and would note that the account will be deleted in 30 days.
# Bolt waits 30 days. During this time, Bolt can investigate whether Bolt has its own reasons not to delete the account (e.g., if there are any debts / damages owed _to Bolt_). If so, Bolt can write to the fleet driver informing them that the account cannot yet be deleted.
# If Bolt hears back from the fleet, Bolt can review what the fleet has said on a case-by-case basis and act accordingly. If the fleet complains that they have an ongoing matter with a fleet driver (and does not cite a compelling legal reason why Bolt should not delete the account), Bolt should respond to the fleet that the matter should be solved outside of Bolt, and the fleet should otherwise use the 30 days to ensure that it has what it needs going forward, as Bolt needs to meet its privacy obligations. If Bolt hears nothing from the fleet, the account can be deleted.

Chances are your question has been already answered in the Knowledge Base. 
https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360016883020

FAQ

Q: Can the Payment OPS issue a refund? 
A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin. 
Rides: refund_payments, customer_support_beehive_ridehailing_order_refund
Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days
Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360016883020

FAQ

Q: Can the Payment OPS issue a refund? 
A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin. 
Rides: refund_payments, customer_support_beehive_ridehailing_order_refund
Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days
Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin. 
Rides: refund_payments, customer_support_beehive_ridehailing_order_refund
Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days
Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

Hi team,

Chances are your question has been already answered in the Knowledge Base. 
https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360016883020

FAQ

Q: Can the Payment OPS issue a refund? 
A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin. 
Rides: refund_payments, customer_support_beehive_ridehailing_order_refund
Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days
Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

Query is prepared:


{noformat}%sql

with user_cohorts as (
    select
    user_id, 
    cohort_lpt as user_cohort, 
    --'lpt' as cohort_methodology,
    date_trunc('week', date) as week,
    home_city_id as city_id
    from ng_public_spark.etl_incentives_rider_targeting_features
    where home_city_id in (1, 3, 9, 10, 11, 18, 25, 54, 55, 74, 79, 136, 137, 150, 211, 242, 271, 320, 324, 325, 326, 329, 334, 335, 343, 386, 437, 813, 862, 881)
    and dayofweek(date) = 2
    and date(date) >= date('2022-10-22')
    and date(date) < date('2024-04-06')
    ),
    

user_orders as (
  SELECT 
    user_id, 
    date_trunc('week', created_date) as week,
    order_city_id as city_id,
    ride_price_before_discounts_eur, -- ride price
    ride_price_after_discounts_eur, --price
    order_id
  FROM core_models_spark.fact_rides_order_try
  WHERE order_city_id in (1, 3, 9, 10, 11, 18, 25, 54, 55, 74, 79, 136, 137, 150, 211, 242, 271, 320, 324, 325, 326, 329, 334, 335, 343, 386, 437, 813, 862, 881)
  and order_try_state = 'finished'
  AND date(created_date) >= date('2022-10-22')
  AND date(created_date) < date('2024-04-06')
)
    
select 
    coalesce(uc.city_id, uo.city_id) as city_id,
    date_format(coalesce(uc.week, uo.week), 'yyyy-MM-dd') as week,
    case when uc.user_cohort is null then 'tourist' else uc.user_cohort end as user_cohort,
    'lpt' as cohort_methodology,
    cast(sum(ride_price_before_discounts_eur) as float) as weekly_gmv_cohort,
    cast(count(uo.order_id) as double) as weekly_finished_orders_cohort,
    count(distinct(coalesce(uc.user_id, uo.user_id))) as user_count,
    cast(sum(case when uo.ride_price_after_discounts_eur / uo.ride_price_before_discounts_eur < 0.99 then uo.ride_price_before_discounts_eur else 0 end) as float) as weekly_gmv_cohort_discounted,
    cast(sum(case when uo.ride_price_after_discounts_eur / uo.ride_price_before_discounts_eur < 0.99 then 1 else 0 end) as float) as weekly_finished_orders_cohort_discounted,
    cast(sum(case when uo.ride_price_after_discounts_eur / uo.ride_price_before_discounts_eur < 0.99 then (uo.ride_price_before_discounts_eur - uo.ride_price_after_discounts_eur) else 0 end) as float) as weekly_bonus_cohort

from user_cohorts as uc
full outer join user_orders as uo
on uc.user_id = uo.user_id
and uc.week = uo.week
and uc.city_id = uo.city_id
and uc.user_id is not null
group by 1,2,3,4 {noformat}

FAQ

Q: Can the Payment OPS issue a refund? 
A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin. 
Rides: refund_payments, customer_support_beehive_ridehailing_order_refund
Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days
Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

My thoughts:

* under *_How can individuals exercise their rights:_* it is mentioned they can access their data (so I assume they can access their photographs). In that case, *_unauthorised use of devices_* should be also checked under *_Information Security Risks Analysis_*. 
** Unauthorised access of account/device → the wrong person requests for access of the data → CS completes the request without knowing the person contacting them is actually not the account owner
** In that case, *_third party_* should also be checked under the main sources that can exploit the vulnerabilities (I understand that this won’t change the risk level in the DPIA as it’s already high, but just in case wanted to highlight to ensure I’ve understood everything correctly here).
* I agree with you regarding user consent. I understand the reasoning for not asking for consent (as this would most likely defeat the purpose of this feature), *but unfortunately none of the other exceptions under article 9 are not applicable, so consent is compulsory for this feature.* I also can’t see any alternatives to this (e.g. giving the user an option to opt-out from that and have their picture reviewed manually by a human instead, as it would not be realistic considering the volumes of new users and the amount of existing users to compare the photographs to).
* Unfortunately I don’t see any reasonable ways to reduce the risk, considering that this feature is meant for fraud prevention. [~accountid:63622ea17d4645af4f03bd18], could you please review my feedback? I believe we should consult the Data Protection Inspectorate on this one.

FAQ

Q: Can the Payment OPS issue a refund? 
A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin. 
Rides: refund_payments, customer_support_beehive_ridehailing_order_refund
Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days
Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

After reading this through again, I think the correct way of naming this is Vouchers, not coupons, as they are clearly those described [here|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1NWVedJuD2oXl-C_Y13NB5k3P_Fgtb-H8SYTtnMc40B4/edit#heading=h.lk38lrrj3m7f]. 

*Type 1:* Code that can be used to pay for ride, *1)* our Bolt Business customer goes to Business Portal where they can create vouchers, *2)* then a voucher code is generated, *3)* Voucher distribution: The Bolt Business customer (in this case Orange and Azziza) sells them to end users (not distributes among its employees, but sells the voucher to individuals) *4)*   Voucher redemption: Type 1, when customer uses it to pay for ride/order *- This is the payment triggering event -* after that we can invoice this Bolt Business customer, *5)* Invoicing customer: For those Bolt Business customers using post payment (as Azziza and Orange would be), cost will be added to next invoice.

As per Fin. Reg Guidelines on Prepaid instruments [here|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1AZ6R3pQcPhwHNTbSdXytaZeG3T1CvIgO0N50WP1DcK4/edit?usp=sharing]: 

It is “Ok to issue instruments that are *post-paid*. For example, voucher codes (code can be used to pay for ride), if payment by Bolt Business customer is made +after+ redemption of the voucher by rider (i.e. rider has purchased goods/services with the voucher).”

Hi team, 
Thank you for escalating the refund issue to Customer Payments team! 

Chances are your question has been already answered in the Knowledge Base. 
https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360016883020

FAQ

Q: Can the Payment OPS issue a refund? 
A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin. 
Rides: refund_payments, customer_support_beehive_ridehailing_order_refund
Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days
Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

Dear *Ciprian,*



Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *19 August 2024.*



After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 



As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example,that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software.Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail,  we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.



We will share copies of the personal data we hold about *you* to which you are entitled. This includes:

* *Order history*



Since it also relates to a third party subject, a passenger, with their pick up and drop off locations displayed, it needs to be regarded as private and confidential, as issued for the purposes of defending a penalty notice received by you and you should process this data only in accordance with the applicable privacy law and cannot use it otherwise, except for defending a penalty.

For information on how we process relevant personal data, we refer you to our Privacy Policy at [https://bolt.eu/en-gb/privacy/|https://bolt.eu/en-gb/privacy/|smart-link], which includes further information about:

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;
* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* Your rights in relation to your personal data;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.



*Your rights* 



In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data,restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 



If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

 

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.





Yours sincerely,

Bolt

FAQ

Q: Can the Payment OPS issue a refund? 
A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin. 
Rides: refund_payments, customer_support_beehive_ridehailing_order_refund
Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days
Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

I've just reviewed the attached _Sondernutzungssatzung_ and the related _Gebührenverzeichnis zur Sondernutzungssatzung_. Unfortunately, it looks like there is no room to challenge (rügen) the fee as demanded by the municipality. The issue is that the _Sondernutzungssatzung_ correctly references the _Gebührenverzeichnis zur Sondernutzungssatzung_, which sets a yearly fee of €90 per scooter. This means the municipality is demanding the correct fee according to their _Sondernutzungssatzung_.

Our only option to contest this would be to directly challenge the initial determination of the fee in the _Gebührenverzeichnis zur Sondernutzungssatzung_. And I beliveve we have these two options first:

*a)Filing an Objection:* First, you should file an objection against the fee notice. This must generally be done within one month of receiving the notice. In the objection, you should provide a detailed explanation of why the fee is considered disproportionately high. It is important to present concrete arguments and, if possible, provide comparisons to similar cases. Here I would need your help assessing why we think this cost is disproportionately high.

*b)Request for Review of the Fee Ordinance:* You can request the municipality to review the legality and appropriateness of the fee ordinance and the associated fee schedule. In this request, you should explain why the fee seems unreasonable and which aspects of proportionality might be violated.

However, assessing the chances of success for such a move is difficult and would likely require external legal counsel.

A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin. 
Rides: refund_payments, customer_support_beehive_ridehailing_order_refund
Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days
Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

Status Update:

Answering to regulator’s questions, waiting for one more confirmation from Software Engineers.

✅  Gathered the evidence AKI requested - the response has 3 attachments

* [Attachment 1|https://drive.google.com/drive/u/0/folders/19TbrbtJ8S1y4ZXStHOwpV3xa9WrzgQ0n]: documentation of DL verification flow supplementing the description of DL verification flow 
* [Attachment 2|https://drive.google.com/drive/u/0/folders/14gocAapIFHxqLzs2A7nLzfbzjrklGPc5]: copies of personal data of the Complainant used to open the additional account + copies of personal data of the Complainant connected to the genuine account + internal investigation evidence
* [Attachment 3|https://drive.google.com/drive/u/0/folders/1p4R-t34JZCCTv18oMrRrSSuZQ_IhtpiD]: conversation transcript between Bolt and the Complainant and Bolt and the fraudster

To comprise the answer, I involved software engineers (Verification) who provided their comments directly into the document. 



Here’s a digest of their comments (of the most relevance to the response to AKI):

{color:#006644}*Reason for letting the fraudster in*{color}

* Bolt switched from external provider’s SDK to its own SDK - Bolt collects user’s data that the external provider verifies
* The fraudster used the so-called man-in-the-middle attack (MitM) due to the weakness of our old verification system that allowed to inject the photo
* Fraudsters found out a way to inject any photos into the verification system
* In February 2024, Bolt enabled a temporary solution to prevent such cases and stronger verification only was enabled for iOS on 25.05.2024 and 08.07.2024 for Android. While the first solution only guaranteed that only the first photo could not be injected, the current solution guarantees that no photos can be injected.

{color:#006644}*Verification flow*{color}

* Bolt checks: the type of document (the driver’s licence), whether that selfie and document are live (i.e. if the photos are not of screens or printouts), that none of the photos are injected, and that selfies match with the document photo.
* Veriff checks: the authenticity and extracts data from the document.
* Description of the normal verification flow: [https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/4514284499/Bolt+Drive+carsharing+via+Verification+SDK+Veriff+API|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/4514284499/Bolt+Drive+carsharing+via+Verification+SDK+Veriff+API|smart-link] 

{color:#006644}*How are we going to prevent future similar incidents (What measures have we taken)*{color}

* Q4: checking documents against the government database (Estonia - pilot)
* Fixed the system that no photos can be injected - ensuring all photos taken are live

{color:#006644}*When/how was user was contacted*{color}

* Process for duplicates: we trigger new verification when new account goes live (does a ride) to the old account.
* If there’s a debt, we do not allow the old account to use the services until they contact us and resolve the issue.



Software engineers (Verification) POCs: Aleksei German, Anna Mitruschniekova, Pavel Nekrasov

Bolt Drive Ops: Mattias Moisto

Hi team, 
Thank you for escalating the refund issue to Customer Payments team! 

Chances are your question has been already answered in the Knowledge Base. 
https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360016883020

FAQ

Q: Can the Payment OPS issue a refund? 
A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin. 
Rides: refund_payments, customer_support_beehive_ridehailing_order_refund
Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days
Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

[~accountid:60e01bd03136170077df0bb9], I’d like to share the outcome of the privacy assessment below. TL;DR we need to obtain user consent and we need to consult Estonian DPA prior to enabling this feature.

*Project Overview* 

The Verification team aims to implement a facial recognition database to prevent fraud and duplicate account creation, particularly from bad actors rejoining the platform after being blocked. The facial recognition process involves four key steps:

# *Image Capture:* Selfies are taken by customers using mobile phone cameras.
# *Feature Extraction:* Algorithms extract key facial features, such as eye distance, nose shape, and face contours, creating a unique facial signature. This information is converted into a numerical code.
# *Comparison:* The extracted features are compared with existing templates in a facial recognition database to identify similarities and differences.
# *Matching and Identification:* If a match is found, the system identifies the individual associated with the stored template. If it is the first capture, the data is stored for future verification. If there is a match, the Bolt Drive Ops team is notified to take action. 

The initial pilot will target Bolt Drive customers, with future expansion planned for Ride Hailing drivers.

h4. *Consent Considerations*

The primary concern is the lack of user consent for this biometric processing. Under Article 9 of the GDPR, processing biometric data is prohibited unless one of the exceptions applies. In this case, none of the exceptions listed in Article 9(2) applies, except for explicit consent, making it the only viable legal basis for this processing activity.

h4. *Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA)*

The DPIA indicates that the project poses a high risk to user privacy. As a result, a prior consultation with the Data Protection Authority (AKI) is mandatory under Article 36 of the GDPR. This consultation process may delay the project by 8 to 14 weeks, as determined by the DPA. [[DPIA - Cognito Form|https://www.cognitoforms.com/bolttechnologyo%C3%BC/dataprotectionimpactassessmentquestionnaire/entries/1-all-entries/34]]

h4. *Relevant Precedent: Clearview AI Fine*

The recent *€30.5 million fine* imposed on Clearview AI by the Dutch Data Protection Authority serves as a critical precedent. Clearview was penalised for creating a vast database of facial images *without consent*, violating GDPR. The fine underscores the severe legal risks associated with non-compliance, particularly regarding biometric data. The case highlights the importance of transparency, user consent, and compliance with GDPR when handling sensitive data like facial biometrics. [[Source|https://autoriteitpersoonsgegevens.nl/actueel/ap-legt-clearview-boete-op-voor-illegale-dataverzameling-voor-gezichtsherkenning?mkt_tok=MTM4LUVaTS0wNDIAAAGVV9HCRcd2uSIRCCxrHXGxekDiD8s-_BljXKy1xyTgjMu3c6hTzU87RXQt6E9MaNErrHSp1xHo2gBGGB6xjubyovIsHdMqb7P0762yruF9AAlw]]

h4. *Conclusion*

Given the high privacy risks, mandatory user consent, and the legal precedent set by the Clearview AI case, the proposed project must proceed with caution. Securing explicit user consent and engaging in a prior consultation with the DPA are essential steps to mitigate the risk of substantial penalties and ensure compliance with GDPR. Other issues to consider:

* Clear retention periods for personal data
* Access rights - data subjects have the right to view their data
* Transparency - information in the Privacy Notice about uses of data subjects’ selfies and biometric data

FAQ

Q: Can the Payment OPS issue a refund? 
A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin. 
Rides: refund_payments, customer_support_beehive_ridehailing_order_refund
Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days
Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

* _Regarding_ *_Germany_*_:_
_The legal assessment on the use of dashcams in Germany remains unchanged from the previous advice. The German Data Protection Authorities are very restrictive about dashcam usage, often more so than the German Federal Court (BGH). While the BGH allows dashcam use within very narrow limits for evidence in accidents, requiring strict privacy measures like short recording times and automatic deletion, the Data Protection Authorities generally consider dashcam use unlawful due to privacy concerns._
_BGH requirements: Dashcams may only be legally used if stringent technical measures are implemented, such as: (i) very short storage periods of the records, (ii) short-term, occasion-based recordings which are only activated by a motion sensor in the event of a collision or severe slow-down of the vehicle (60-120 seconds), (iii) pixelation of persons and (iv) automatic deletion outside the control of the dashcam user._

[~accountid:5ed4b18fc3b5390c24a6f905] and [~accountid:5d0c8f1621a5d30bc4e096a8] since the risk review, we have begun the terminology adjustment from ‘blocks’ to *suspensions* but we did agree to hold off on changing anything else. 

Please see my proposals for blocking terminology change which are based on Legal team’s feedback: 

* Warning (Informative message warning that repetitive behaviour may get the account suspended/terminated) - Keep *Warning* as it exists now in the Blocking Matrix, and *replace Educate* as an outcome with *Warning*. * Termination (permanent suspension)

How it works in Admin (and how it’s worded) we can not change too much, but I agree with tying ‘terminating the account’ with the Partner-level block for couriers and drivers, and amending the guidelines so it’s clear. 

Additionally, not quite sure why they are asking for guidelines to set the Partner Status: Hidden. We should not be doing that if the driver needs to be hard-blocked. Will clarify this once we agree

Please let me know what you think
