~ I. Summary of the events ~

Short Summary: On 26 August 2024, Mr. Siyabonga Makhoba reported to the Customer Support that he was unable to access his driver account. He indicated that his login details, including email ([mackoberlian@gmail.com|mailto:mackoberlian@gmail.com]) and phone number (0790527934), no longer worked. He expressed concern that his account had been hacked and that unauthorised changes were made, preventing him from working for the past two weeks. Despite multiple attempts to reset his password, he was unable to regain access. The phone number and email address have been changed in this communication - [https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/428750802|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/428750802]. 

The issue involves several Beehive tickets that have been summarised below:

# [First Communication|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/428991497] - 26.08.2024 - The user, Siyabonga Cleopas Makhoba, has reported that their Bolt account appears to be hacked, preventing them from logging in since the day before. Despite attempting to reset the password and use the "Forgot Password" and "Email me a login link" options, they have not received any emails or SMS messages. CS agent has responded with instructions to reset the password and advised patience since he exercised too many login attempts. However, the user continued to face issues, including messages about being on a trip even though they were not working, and has not received any help resolving the problem.
# [Second communication|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/429172035] - the driver provides screenshots, repeating the content of the first communication - his account has been stoled and he does not have access to username, password, and email address must have been changed as well. He says that he does not receive any verification messages or emails, even after attempting to reset their password and use the "forgot password" and "magic link" options. He is frustrated because the issue has persisted for several days, and they have not received any effective assistance from support.
# [Third communication|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/433136201] - 03.09.2024 - similar content but frustration increases - driver again claims to have lost his username, password, cellphone number or even email address. He additionally says that his only cellphone were ‘Tecno Mobile Stylo device and before he had been using Samsung A14’.
# [Fourth Communication|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/432987532] - The driver was inquired about the device he was using prior to being signed out and whether he had shared his login details or any one-time passwords with anyone outside of Bolt, including through email, in-app messages, or social media. The driver was again advised to attempt logging into the account; however, despite not possessing the correct credentials, the app indicated that the account was currently in use during an active ride, making it temporarily inaccessible for login. He claimed that his details were: [mackoberlian@gmail.com|mailto:mackoberlian@gmail.com], phone number - 0790527934, username: Siyoba413. Today (05.09.2024), a CS agent brought back his back details.

*~ II. Observations ~*

For more than a week, that individual alarms the CS that he had lost access to the account, and cannot regain it since all account’s details must have been changed. Nevertheless, this is the response he was repeatedly receiving - “Thank you for your response. The email you are using to reach out to us here is for a rider, not a driver. Hence, you are advised to reach out to us using your driver account”. *It is not the first time, therefore, what is to be done about it*?

*~ III. Admin’s Portal Investigation ~*

# Since July 17, 2024, 14 different devices have been logged into the account. 

*~ IV. Recommended Actions ~*

Confirm with the CS if he has access back to the account. Then, let’s try to close it off. Entrusted communication. Then, record it.

Thanks [~accountid:63fe21787c30bbd6b33e09d3] - I have spoken with [~accountid:63622ea17d4645af4f03bd18] and we are aligned on the position I set out below. In summary:

* Article 17(3)(e) of the GDPR sets out an exception to complying with an individual’s erasure request - Bolt (as controller) can refuse to do so where the processing is necessary for the establishment, exercise or defence of legal claims.
* Given that the complainant has explicitly stated that “_there could be other incidents that could occur and we wish to pursue bolt for those claims_”, there is a realistic prospect of future litigation here, and the information that the complainant wants deleted may be material to that litigation.
* In light of this, it appears defensible for Bolt to rely on Article 17(3)(e) and +*not*+ delete this information. In our response to the complainant, we can include the following language to address this:

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
“_We have reviewed your request and determined that applicable data protection law permits us to deny your erasure request because the processing is necessary for the establishment, exercise or defence of legal claims._”
{panel}

*PRIVACY ANALYSIS*

* Having reviewed an example of the documents to be shared, they concern a response to the HU tax authority about the transactions between Bolt and a Hungarian company (presumably a fleet). The response contains a breakdown of invoices / commission, trips, bank details etc. It appears to contain the personal data of one driver (presumably the fleet owner) - as such, the personal data seems to be {color:#36b37e}+*limited / low risk*+{color}. However, this is {color:#4c9aff}+*worth double-checking*+{color}. 
* In terms of legal basis, Bolt can defensibly argue that it has a legitimate interest in sharing this kind of information with its partners to ensure the effective running of its business. Indeed, Bolt wants to maintain a good relationship with the HU partner here. As such, Bolt has a {color:#36b37e}+*valid legal basis*+{color} to share the information.
* The currently live driver privacy notice could be more robust with respect to covering this kind of data processing activity, but there is enough in there to defensibly argue that we are transparent about this kind of data sharing. As such, this issue is {color:#36b37e}+*not a blocker*+{color} to the proposed action.
* No data sharing agreement in place with the HU partner. We would ordinarily push for this in order to protect Bolt’s position. However, the lack of a DSA does not necessarily create a non-compliance risk, and the partnership agreement contains general obligations for Bolt to cooperate in good faith with the HU partner in any event. As such, although this is not ideal, it is {color:#36b37e}+*not a blocker*+{color} to the proposed action.

*Conclusion*: From a privacy perspective, we are {color:#36b37e}+*ok with sharing*+{color} the information as suggested, provided that the personal data at-issue is indeed low risk.

A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund.

#  On the data privacy section, please share the below with NBC:

_We have reviewed the NBC Services Agreement and regret to inform that Bolt cannot sign the proposed Schedule 4 on data protection, as it does not accurately reflect the data processing arrangement between Bolt and NBC._

_To be clear, Bolt operates as an independent data controller when providing services to its business customers. Our General Terms and Conditions for Bolt Business Section 4 states explicitly that Bolt and the business customer maintain their independent data controller roles for personal data processing. Bolt fully assumes responsibility for its processing activities and adherence to applicable laws, including the GDPR and local Tanzanian laws._

_Please note that the notion of controllership in our arrangement is cemented by the EDPB Guidelines 07/2020 on the concepts of controller and processor in the GDPR. Specifically, p. 27 para. 82 demonstrates this via “Example: Taxi service”. While Bolt operates as an online platform rather than providing taxi services directly, the example still effectively clarifies the logic underpinning the controller relationship._

_To accurately reflect the arrangement, we've proposed revisions to Schedule 4. These revisions include a clause that clearly states Bolt's responsibility as a separate data controller for its own data processing activities._

_We appreciate your attention and trust that this explanation has clarified any concerns or questions you may have._

Hi [~accountid:61c02e8de7637900682fe2b2] 

it seems that a similar category has been already launched in PT and Romania. 

In particular re Romania:

* Bolt Assist was introduced in RO due to a new law passed earlier this year which states that taxis and ride-hailing companies cannot refuse passengers with disabilities or guide dogs. 
* Discrimination is a sensitive issue in Romania. 
* There is no booking fee or bonus for drivers. However, drivers do receive a reduced commission for these bookings.
* Drivers are given this option automatically, but they can opt out just like any other option. By reducing the commission, Ops is trying to persuade them not to opt out. The price for passengers is the same, but Bolt covers the driver’s efforts by offering a lower commission.

You might want to liaise with RO Ops team to check out the details. Perhaps you can use the same workaround to launch the category in FR with no need to increase the price paid by passengers which could on one hand puts Bolt at risk of being fined by a Consumer protection body or a discrimination body such as Défenseur des Droits and on the other hand undermines the attractiveness of the category as such.

Thanks,

Michela

Thanks [~accountid:5e3d437d9749d00c924cb0f5] - I have reviewed the processes and my thoughts are as follows. The main takeaway here is to make it extra clear what privacy escalation examples may look like in each case, to improve process clarity and to ensure that only relevant cases are being escalated. Happy to discuss if this is unclear! 🙂 

----

[I want to know why my rating dropped|https://www.figma.com/board/1tiA6Kz7zj9hF3wq5HCBWn/I-want-to-know-why-my-Rider-rating-dropped?node-id=0-1&t=Utsw1hMoaJRJ0rJv-1]

* For the “_Examples of when to escalate to privacy_”, I would make the following minor tweaks:
** “_The rider is concerned about_ {color:#ff5630}_rider_{color} _rating visibility_ {color:#ff5630}_(either to the rider themselves or_{color} _to drivers_{color:#ff5630}_)_{color}”
** “The rider is concerned about their rating for {color:#ff5630}-a-{color} specific trip{color:#ff5630}s{color} or wants all their previous rating data {color:#ff5630}(beyond their average rider rating){color}“
* When referring the user to the blog post and the Marketplace Conduct Guidelines (“*MCG*”), we should make clear in the process that we are referring the user to the _blog post_ as this explains how the rider rating feature works, whereas the _MCG_ will give the user tips on how to behave in a way that could improve their rating (i.e., we should not give the impression that the MCG explains how the feature works).
* Otherwise, I have no additional comments.

----

[I want to increase my rider rating|https://www.figma.com/board/It4FQySTk3FlZlFNy5JWLY/I-want-to-increase-my-Rider-rating?node-id=0-1&t=M26cNvygL9SKpOyY-1]

* As with the ‘I want to know why my rating dropped’ process, I think it is worth including a second branch which covers when such requests should be escalated to privacy. 
** Although examples would be limited, _technically_ a rider could make this request and mention personal data processing / data protection law, and so we should ensure that the process covers this. 
** In terms of the “_Examples of when to escalate to privacy_”, I would mainly draw attention to “_Issues / requests / questions that explicitly mention either: (a) data protection law; and/or (b) personal data processing_”, and specifically flag as an example “_I would like you to correct my rider rating per my rights under Article 16 of the GDPR_”.
* As above, we should be clear on why we are referring the user to the blog post and the MCG.
* Otherwise, I have no additional comments.

----

[I want to know more about rider rating|https://www.figma.com/board/9NgWXk1yAbTTizxFtTZ4z8/I-want-to-know-more-about-my-Rider-Rating?node-id=1-58&t=ImwCPX6ao87g1d7U-1]

* As above, I think it is worth including a second branch which covers when such requests should be escalated to privacy. 
** Again, examples here would be limited, but these types of requests may not always be clearly phrased, and so there may be a bit of overlap with 'I want to know why my rating dropped'. As such, we should include the same “_Examples of when to escalate to privacy_” as for that process.
** In particular, when setting out the example of “_Issues / requests / questions that explicitly mention either: (a) data protection law; and/or (b) personal data processing_”, I would specifically flag the example “_How is my personal data processed to calculate my average rating”._
* Otherwise, I have no additional comments.

Hi team,

FAQ

Q: Can the Payment OPS issue a refund? 
A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin. 
Rides: refund_payments, customer_support_beehive_ridehailing_order_refund
Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days
Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

Hi [~accountid:712020:a7a7d4bc-10ca-44a0-a22e-fa8752330abd] - I will include this in tomorrow’s handover, but some quick background here:

* Bolt is entering into a [collaboration agreement|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1GZSD3Hf8CIUxhXybjJlm1uGF4kintPBI5HT7QRMZm6c/edit] with Louwman. Louwman will provide Bolt drivers with discounts on cars provided by Louwman’s dealers. We have been asked whether a data processing / sharing agreement is needed here.
* Based on the responses to Qs we have received to date, it seems that Bolt will not be sharing driver data with Louwman. Rather, Bolt will include on the landing page a link to the offer on Louwman’s website, the driver will follow that link and then provide their own details to Louwman so as to benefit from the offer. As such, not data processing / sharing agreement is needed from the Bolt side to cover this.
* However, we have also been told that Bolt intends to track the performance of this offer. Unfortunately, we have not yet been provided with enough information on how this will work in practice (and what data will be shared to do so). I have sent a follow-up Q on this in [this slack thread|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C07KNSF8VMH/p1725362611090539].
* Otherwise, we have been told that this is all happening in the EU.

My thoughts on {color:#36b37e}*next steps*{color} are as follows:

* Roman’s response on the Slack thread will determine whether a DPA / DSA is required. What I expect will be the outcome here is that Roman will tell us something like Louwman intends to share the total number of Bolt drivers that have taken up the offer with Bolt - if this is the case, no agreement is required. Otherwise, our next steps will be fact-dependent.
* In any event, this is all happening in the EU, so no international data transfer mechanisms are needed here.
* When we provide our final advice to the team, I would re-flag that Clause 3.0 of the [collaboration agreement|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1GZSD3Hf8CIUxhXybjJlm1uGF4kintPBI5HT7QRMZm6c/edit] says “_By activating this offer by the participant in the Bolt platform, the lead will be passed on to the Toyota dealer responsible for this service area. By activating this, the participant agrees to the sharing of his contact details in accordance with the General Personal Data Regulation_”. I do not think this should be in the agreement, as drivers are not party to it, and so it does not make sense to me - as such, unless you disagree, we should push for this to be removed.

https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360016883020

FAQ

Q: Can the Payment OPS issue a refund? 
A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin. 
Rides: refund_payments, customer_support_beehive_ridehailing_order_refund
Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days
Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

Chances are your question has been already answered in the Knowledge Base. 
https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360016883020

FAQ

Q: Can the Payment OPS issue a refund? 
A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin. 
Rides: refund_payments, customer_support_beehive_ridehailing_order_refund
Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days
Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

# *Top-Up Functionality:* Although Bolt Balance has not been officially launched in Thailand, some users have managed to successfully top-up through the Transaction History page.

Given that these issues are not the users' fault, the Bolt Balance should not be negative. To address the immediate concerns, we’ve allowed all agents to refund users by selecting Bolt as the actor.

Hi team,

Chances are your question has been already answered in the Knowledge Base. 
https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360016883020

FAQ

Q: Can the Payment OPS issue a refund? 
A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin. 
Rides: refund_payments, customer_support_beehive_ridehailing_order_refund
Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days
Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

I am tagging you in this ticket because I have observed a certain pattern, which seems concerning from Privacy side, especially in cases of *account sharing*. As outlined in the investigation below, the current process allows for changing important account details, such as email addresses, phone numbers, or bank accounts, simply by communicating through Beehive.

The issue arises when this process is misused, with individuals requesting multiple changes within a short timeframe. In the case below, and in previous instances, the driver changed their email address and phone number *five times* in just two weeks. This raises the question of whether we should introduce CS guidelines to limit or flag situations where drivers request too many detail changes in-app within a specific period. As I understand, there are currently no restrictions in place for these types of requests, except when a related Beehive communication is ongoing.

Thus, let me know what is your opinion on that and what could we do potentially to prevent such instances.

[~accountid:5df3830c73b0bd0e4d835499] this is a tricky road to take, as saying “using BKY = privacy risk” and continuing to use their services means that we are using a non-compliant provider. Also, it is our obligation to make sure we do not enter into a relationship with a non-compliant provider in the first place + we need to make sure that we have a proper data sharing agreement in place, because this responsibility is put on the data controller’s (i.e. Bolt’s) shoulders.

However, as we have now spotted an issue with BKY - i.e. lack of compliant data sharing agreement - we need/want to fix it, which is in the best interest of Bolt/drivers.



All this legalese aside, let me answer your questions:

* _Does the use of BKY constitute a privacy risk?_
** *Yes*. We clearly see that personal data is being shared between Bolt<>BKY. So, under GDPR, we are obligated to enter into a data sharing agreement (DSA), which has to lay out our responsibilities/obligations/data security questions/other relevant topics.
** We currently do not have it, which puts us at risk.
** While it’s our and their fault that we have not signed the DSA initially, it is the responsibility of both parties to have it signed now. We want to do it, but BKY disagrees by stating that they do not do “data processing”, which they clearly do.
* _Can we use the attached email to showcase that the use of BKY constitutes a privacy risk?_
** It’s not a privacy question per-se, but I would not give the copy of the email to a third party, but I’d stick to mentioning that BKY disagrees with our offer to sign a DSA, which poses a privacy risk to us. The reason behind not sharing an email copy is because it might be considered confidential, but perhaps [~accountid:712020:7f47c2af-14e1-4206-a795-ac87cb906276] can comment on this.

It is still unclear what Tesco means by “What rules for the personal data protection do customers follow?”. I’d suggest we respond that as per Section 2.1. of the Schedule 2 of our T&Cs, both parties (as separate data controllers) ensure compliance with the applicable data protection laws. This means that  for example to us, GDPR and relevant national data protection law applies. The main consequence for customers is what supervisory authority they can complain to in case they suspect that their rights have been violated during the processing of the personal data by either party. If it relates to processing done on Bolt side,  the customers complain to Estonian DPI (or Czech DPI that forwards the complaint to Estonian DPI). If customers complain in relation to processing on Tesco’s side, it would be vice-versa.

Please, ask if this response is sufficient or if they could clarify what did they mean so that we can provide more appropriate answer.

+Regarding point 5 (direct marketing)+

When parties to the agreement use the shared data (listed in point 2) for direct marketing (which none of the parties is prevented from) - each party to the agreement takes care of the lawfulness of processing the shared persona; data for direct marketing. This includes but is not limited to having a legal basis, obtains consent (if necessary), and allows data subjects (customers) to exercise their rights under the applicable data protection laws (e.g. opt out from direct marketing).

Hi team,

Chances are your question has been already answered in the Knowledge Base. 
https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360016883020

FAQ

Q: Can the Payment OPS issue a refund? 
A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin. 
Rides: refund_payments, customer_support_beehive_ridehailing_order_refund
Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days
Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

FAQ

Q: Can the Payment OPS issue a refund? 
A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin.

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

We’re able to display the wished ‘nickname’ as per the driver’s request, but we are also obliged to show to real name as per the clause you brought out. The definition for the operator is _any person, whether natural or legal, who is authorised by the Authority to operate either a light passenger transport service or a vehicle hire service, or both._ 

My interpretation of this is that we need to show the contact details that have been registered with the Authorities in Malta. So if she is registered there with her old name still then we need to also comply with that. But, as mentioned, the workaround would be adding the ‘nickname’. I have also confirmed with Product Legal that there are no EU level restrictions to this. 

At the moment I would draft a response where I would bring out that we are able to add the second name, but to comply with local legislation we would still need to keep the old name visible for the riders as well.

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. * The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;

Hi team,

Chances are your question has been already answered in the Knowledge Base. 
https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360016883020

FAQ

Q: Can the Payment OPS issue a refund? 
A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin. 
Rides: refund_payments, customer_support_beehive_ridehailing_order_refund
Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days
Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

Hi team, 
Thank you for escalating the refund issue to Customer Payments team! 

Chances are your question has been already answered in the Knowledge Base. 
https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360016883020

FAQ

Q: Can the Payment OPS issue a refund? 
A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin. 
Rides: refund_payments, customer_support_beehive_ridehailing_order_refund
Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days
Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

* Any high-priority event reported to Bolt and subsequently escalated on social media.

h3. Handling Threats Involving TFL:

Hello! 

We already do biometric post-processing in the Verification system: to automatically match faces. For this, a couple of years ago we started gathering user consents. You can read more details here [https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PRODWIKI/pages/3871768748/Driver+Selfie+Verification#Biometric-Consent|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PRODWIKI/pages/3871768748/Driver+Selfie+Verification#Biometric-Consent|smart-link] and here [https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/4100654651/User+consent+for+biometric+data+processing|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/4100654651/User+consent+for+biometric+data+processing|smart-link]. In short: 

* we ask a user for consent if we want to automatically match user faces. If a user provides consent we match faces using an automatic algorithm. Otherwise, a real person compares 2 photos manually.
* if a user provided consent once, we reuse their consent in future verifications.
* if a user did not provide a consent, we ask them for consent every time.
* to determine if a user’s selfie is live (face is present on the photo, it is not a photo of a photo or a photo of a screen) we do not ask a user for consent. The machine model tries to determine it automatically and only if it fails, we fallback to a manual check

Now I have a few questions:

# For the DB of faces projects, can we use faces, for which we received user consent?
# If we can use only photos of the users, who provided consent it kills the purpose of the project: detect fraud. The reason is that fraudsters can simply not provide consent to us and hence we won’t be able to detect duplicates. How can we resolve it?
## Is there a legal way for us to eventually process photos without consent?
## if not, can we stop serving users, who do not provide a consent? Meaning that if a user does not provide a consent, we do not verify them and, in the result, they cannot use Bolt services: rentals, ride-hailing etc. Is it legal to do so?
# We found a bug today - it turned out that 
## in some flows we do not ask consent, although we should
## in some other flows we ask users for consent but we ignore it (whatever the user has chosen we proceed with an automatic algorithm)
## We are going to fix these bugs but it looks like a Privacy incident. Should I report it somewhere? What should be our action points after we fix a bug?

* we only have one relevant offer which is gasoline discount. If we will go by Bolt Rewards level distribution we will lose majority of active gasoline cards.

* Our main goal with this partnership is to be the *only ride-hailing platform which have contract with biggest gasoline company* in Croatia. In that why its locked from uber but we need to hit targets.

* Relevancy of the pilot and correct distribution of cards

* If its AB test we still dont know which 50% of drivers have bolt rewards since admin if providing list of all drivers. Each monday, lates tuseday we need to send new distribution of cards.
* Due to all above, we have created standard card distribution which was not connected to the bolt rewards.

Bolt Rewards is a great tool to increase driver activity but in order to work we need to add more offers after which we can consider losing only offer (gasoline company). Internal system benefits are also awesome but main benefit of showing price is already planned for whole Croatia. 
Once we will have more offers we will be ready to test it again correctly.

Thank you for providing more information. 

However, we will still not be making any changes because of the following: 

* We have a detailed [process|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/53202] that must be followed before adding the cleaning fee to the price. CS must confirm a lot of things, which leaves nearly *no room for error* (incorrectly added cleaning fee). 
* If CS follows the mentioned process, confirms that the rider did indeed made a mess in the driver’s vehicle, and agrees with the driver that the cleaning fee should be compensated, but then receives a different story from the rider and chooses to believe the rider’s version, it will result “*he-said-she-said*” situations and will create even more confusion and additional customer contacts, as the driver will be left confused why the earlier agreed cleaning fee was taken away.

The current process is very thorough and there should not be anything for the user to dispute. If cleaning fee was added, that is done and there should be no refunds.

Hi team,

FAQ

Q: Can the Payment OPS issue a refund? 
A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin. 
Rides: refund_payments, customer_support_beehive_ridehailing_order_refund
Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days
Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

Hi! [~accountid:6052891645a3bb006808f764] lets discuss this topic during our next 1:1. 

In summary, the business wants to know in in which cases we are obliged to refund and what is the limit of time a customer has to request a refund. The aim is for the business to be able to reject old refund requests. 

Our competitor has a global approach to this. 

The answer to that is of course it depends on the market. However, from a global perspective, it is totally possible to define an internla litim according to the business risk appetite. For this, we should consider:

* What are the regulations around refunds in each market. Meaning:
** Is there an obligation to refund applicable to our services?
** In this same context, what is the limit of time a customer can request a refund according to their consumers law?
* Card Scheme Rules and the rules in regard to chargebacks. A cardholder can request a chargeback within 120/80 days (Visa and MC have different deadlines) after the payment. 
* What competitors do (Uber). They have a limit of 30 days after the completion of the order to ask for a refund. After that is up to them to decide. This is a global policy.

Hey [~accountid:712020:770b0a51-ce61-48b4-990c-622be4e099ce], 

{quote}After safety related issue is resolved should the Agent change severity level to Tier 1 and None, and then deal with non-safety issue or not, as this becomes a non-safety issue.{quote}

If a case contains both a safety and a non-safety issue, the case doesn’t become a non-safety case once the safety part is solved. If it’s a safety case, the severity shouldn’t be removed unless a process states otherwise. The same goes for issue tags. The tier can change depending on whether the agent who initially handled the case is trained to deal with non-safety issues or not. If yes - the case remains in the safety tier with the applicable severity even if there is a non-safety issue, but the agent should add the relevant non-safety issue tags. If the agent is not trained to solve the non-safety part - the case needs to be escalated to Tier 1, but the severity will not change, and safety issue tags will remain on the case. Tier 1 agent will add the relevant non-safety tags. 

As mentioned before, we’re revamping all of the safety workflows, including the safety escalation guidelines. * Links on the cookie declaration page were made more noticeable so it is easier to click.

# The Cookie Banner is now compliant with EU and UK regulatory guidelines and regulations.

{noformat}for num in 325 326 297 802 462 271 1 435 401 463 454 442 1052 324 1053 158 350 1049 3; do mkdir $num; aws s3 cp --recursive s3://taxify-maps-data/live/models/bolt-maps-routing/v1.3/2024-08-31-04-10-49/cities/$num $num; done
osmium merge 1/city.osm.pbf 1049/city.osm.pbf 1052/city.osm.pbf 1053/city.osm.pbf 158/city.osm.pbf 271/city.osm.pbf 297/city.osm.pbf 3/city.osm.pbf 324/city.osm.pbf 325/city.osm.pbf 326/city.osm.pbf 350/city.osm.pbf 401/city.osm.pbf 435/city.osm.pbf 442/city.osm.pbf 454/city.osm.pbf 462/city.osm.pbf 463/city.osm.pbf 802/city.osm.pbf -o output/merged.pbf
DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=$(pwd) ./osrm-extract output/merged.pbf -p /Users/octavianmoraru/repos/taxify/bolt-osrm-backend/profiles/car.lua 
DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=$(pwd) ./osrm-partition output/merged.osrm
DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=$(pwd) ./osrm-customize output/merged.osrm
DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=$(pwd) ./osrm-routed --algorithm mld output/merged.osrm -p 9876

The current flow:

* ride starts: authorize (for APMs capture in fact) e.g. 50 EUR
* ride finishes: real price e.g. 40 EUR
* booking service requests capture form payments for 40 EUR
* payments will do partial refund for 10 EUR
* payments will publish update status event with capture for 40 EUR
* booking checks that requested capture and actual capture amount are the same and takes no action (otherwise there would be negative/positive balance created)

instead we could do:

* ride starts: authorize (for APMs capture in fact) e.g. 50 EUR
* ride finishes: real price e.g. 40 EUR
* booking service requests capture form payments for 40 EUR
* *payments will publish update status event with capture for 50 EUR*
* *booking service requests refund to the original payment method for 10 EUR*
** not considering any negative/positive balance the user might have otherwise
* *payments refund 10 EUR to the original payment method*

booking would have to refund to the original payment method (not to balance), but the records capture would be for 50 EUR (the desired result of the change). 

…. just a suggestion.

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin. 
Rides: refund_payments, customer_support_beehive_ridehailing_order_refund
Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days
Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

Pls note that blocking associated with low passenger score has been addressed in the Uber case and the Court held that the feature showed a degree of control of the platform over the drivers pushing them to increase the quality of the transportation services provided.

see below the relevant wording

“Le chauffeur doit également veiller à maintenir une évaluation moyenne par les utilisateurs supérieure à l’évaluation minimale moyenne fixée par Uber. L’évaluation par les utilisateurs est utilisée ici comme un instrument de surveillance de chaque prestation des chauffeurs, incitant ceux-ci à tout faire pour maintenir une note élevée sous peine de risquer d’être exclus de la plateforme. (_Commission, 26/10/2020, décision Uber_)”

In light of the above and considering the ongoing inspection in BE I recommend to put this initiative on hold.

https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360016883020

FAQ

Q: Can the Payment OPS issue a refund? 
A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin. 
Rides: refund_payments, customer_support_beehive_ridehailing_order_refund
Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days
Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin. 
Rides: refund_payments, customer_support_beehive_ridehailing_order_refund
Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days
Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

FAQ

Q: Can the Payment OPS issue a refund? 
A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin. 
Rides: refund_payments, customer_support_beehive_ridehailing_order_refund
Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days
Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

Chances are your question has been already answered in the Knowledge Base. 
https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360016883020

FAQ

Q: Can the Payment OPS issue a refund? 
A: No, Payment OPS don't have an access to issue a refund in Beehive or in Admin. 

Q: I would like to issue a refund, but I don't have the necessary accesses. 
A: Your team lead should have permissions to issue refunds. Please escalate to them. If they are lacking any permissions then you can apply for the following in Admin. 
Rides: refund_payments, customer_support_beehive_ridehailing_order_refund
Delivery: Refund old orders (delivery_order_refund_extended) after 30 days
Rentals: rental_order_refund, rental_subscriptions_refund, rental_order_refund_city_fine
Carsharing: rental_car_order_refund
Bolt+: subscription_offer_customer_support

Q: Customer requests a refund to the original payment method. 
A: If you have already issued a refund to the Bolt Balance, but the customer is requesting a refund to OPM. You need to force the refund to Original payment method. We are not able to remove the balance. The customer will receive a double-refund. 

Q: Can I refund after Chargebacks?
A: No. If the customer has received a chargeback then we are not able to issue a refund. 

If this solved your issue then we will close the ticket in 5 days. 
If you would still like the payment operations team to take a look at this issue then please leave a comment on the ticket and we will not close the case.

Hi [~accountid:712020:548c71a6-d1f4-404d-9c5e-482bc0de371a] , CCI team has no feedback for the MSA and DPA agreement. However, they shared some feedback regarding Clause 2.6 (Material Breach & Penalty) in the SLA doc. They are not OK with this line in the SLA doc: 

_Not meeting the KPI requirements set out in this Agreement for 2 consecutive months will be deemed a material breach of this Agreement._

According to CCI, they have several issues with accepting KPI miss as a material breach. 

# The overall headcount (team size) is just 8 FTEs which is not enough to meet Turn Around Time target for all workflows.
# We do not have proper reporting / dashboards in place to give visibility to TAT / Backlog on a realtime basis or a daily basis which makes it difficult for the team to manage performance and commit to zero backlog.
# There are no proper tools (task management tool / WFM tools) in place. Team lead has to manually assign tasks to agents and keep moving agents from one workflow to the other depending on the volume. 

We (I, Kirill, Linda) agree with CII and we are aligned to not consider KPI miss as a material breach till we have sufficient headcount and proper reporting and tolling in place. 

Please find attached doc with the revised wording proposed by CCI. 

Let me know if you have any questions / feedback. If you are aligned, we can proceed with sending the contract for final signature.

{quote}_Dear _,_

_Thank you for your recent inquiry regarding the circumstances under which Bolt obtained your consent. We recognise the importance of GDPR compliance and are committed to ensuring that your rights as a data subject are fully respected._

_In this context, we consider your inquiry as a Data Subject Request (DSR) under GDPR. Typically, such requests are initiated by the data subject themselves. However, we acknowledge the possibility of authorised representatives acting on behalf of the data subject._

_To address your concern, we have forwarded your request to our privacy team, who will provide you with the relevant information within the legally prescribed timeframe. The privacy team will respond to you directly from_ [_privacy@bolt.eu_|mailto:privacy@bolt.eu]_.
